_comment: Hand-authored album metadata. The tuning system lives in the DIRECTORY name and nowhere in the filenames, so it cannot be derived — it has to be recorded here. `scripts/build-catalog.mjs` merges this with the track lists scanned from ~/Dropbox/Uploads and writes src/data/catalog.json, which IS committed (Cloudflare's build machine has no Dropbox access).
_review: Entries marked "needsReview": true are Prent's to confirm — the tuning/blurb was inferred from the directory name, not from anything authoritative.

albums.title: August 2026
albums.blurb: The current rotation — the album the daily post draws from.

albums.title: Short Repeats
albums.blurb: A structural variant with the repeats shortened.

albums.title: Werckmeister III
albums.blurb: The same twelve chorales in Werckmeister III, the well temperament of Bach's own era — a reference point between equal temperament and just intonation.

albums.title: 12-Tone Equal Temperament
albums.blurb: The control. The same twelve chorales in the tuning of every modern piano, for direct comparison.

albums.title: Original Bach
albums.blurb: Earlier renders, using the legacy max-shift setting rather than the density control.

just.label: Just intonation
just.description: Chords tuned to whole-number frequency ratios drawn from a tonality diamond, found by simulated annealing and then threaded together with Viterbi optimisation.

12tet.label: 12-tone equal temperament
12tet.description: The modern standard: the octave split into twelve identical steps. Every key is equally usable and no chord is perfectly in tune.

werckmeister.label: Werckmeister III
werckmeister.description: A well temperament from 1691, contemporary with Bach. Keys retain distinct character rather than sounding identical.
